# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Platform and task adaptation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the person’s primary task and the target platform before translating a screen. Read that platform’s procedure; use Principles to resolve hierarchy and Designing for games only for gameplay.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ios
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPhone experience for handheld touch, interrupted use, orientation changes, and system entrypoints.

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

# Make television choices visible from across the room

Read [Designing for tvOS](../../references/designing-for-tvos.md). Inspect the primary activity, content hierarchy, viewer/profile model, authentication, and input assumptions. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode and use supplied evidence to separate confirmed defects from untested remote behavior.

Rebuild the hierarchy around distant viewing and focus navigation. Prioritize legible titles and recognizable imagery rather than filling the TV with desktop density. Map directional movement and selection from each major region. The focused item must visibly identify both location and the available action through the platform's focus treatment; do not leave essential navigation dependent on pointer hover or tiny touch targets.

Choose the appropriate input contract. Siri Remote must support ordinary browsing; games may add controllers and relevant companion/voice input. Avoid making controller possession necessary for non-controller tasks. For long sessions or picture-in-picture, preserve the person's place when attention changes.

Reduce repetitive authentication using appropriate system integration. If the current system viewer changes, switch to the matching app profile deliberately and preserve privacy boundaries. Add Top Shelf, TV-app discovery, provider support, or SharePlay only when the content/activity warrants it, with a destination that matches the selected item.

**Before → decision → after:** A cooking-video app uses small tab labels, pointer hover menus, and one permanently signed-in household profile. Decision: across-room remote browsing and changing viewers require explicit focus routes and profile ownership. After, clear focusable categories lead into large recipe artwork, Select starts the highlighted recipe, and a viewer change updates saved recipes instead of exposing another person's history.

Deliver a focus-route map and corrected screen/profile flow or implementation. Fail if focus is invisible, a region has no remote exit, or a viewer change retains another profile's personal content. Check actual remote traversal, television legibility, and focus enlargement on supported hardware; a desktop screenshot only supports visual hypotheses.

For detailed movement use [Focus and selection](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) and [Remotes](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md); for shared viewing use [SharePlay](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-shareplay/SKILL.md).

# Designing for iOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. An iPhone experience must work both during brief checks on the move and through extended games, browsing, or media sessions. People switch among apps frequently. ## Best practices - Design for a medium-sized, dense display viewed at roughly 1–2 feet, usually held in one or both hands. Accommodate portrait and landscape use. - Keep primary content and actions clear, with secondary operations reachable through a small number of interactions rather than many simultaneous controls. - Support touch gestures, onscreen keyboards, and voice; use motion sensors, nearby spatial interactions, or personal information only where they improve the task. - Put frequent touch controls within comfortable reach, commonly the middle or lower display. Preserve swipe-back navigation and list-row gestures. - Adapt to orientation, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type without breaking context. - With permission, use platform data and services to reduce typing: location, biometric authentication, and payments are examples. - Integrate appropriate system entry points: widgets, Home Screen quick actions, Spotlight search, Shortcuts, and activity views. Their familiar behavior helps people act outside the main app. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

# Designing for tvOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Design for a large high-resolution screen often viewed from 8 feet or farther away, including by people moving around the room. Entertainment, games, fitness, education, and home utility experiences can hold attention for hours; picture in picture can coexist with another activity. ## Best practices - Make the entire interface legible and understandable across the room. Use rich edge-to-edge imagery, subtle fluid motion, and engaging audio for a cinematic result. - Work with Siri Remote gestures and the tvOS focus system. A clear focused item should highlight and enlarge as people navigate so location and available action stay apparent. - Accommodate game controllers, voice, and companion-device apps as appropriate inputs. - Make authentication infrequent and easy. Support shared sign-in and switch the app’s profile when the system’s current viewer changes. - Integrate TV-app discovery, SharePlay, Top Shelf, and TV-provider account support when relevant. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 14, 2022.

# Keep the interaction target distinct from the chosen value

Read [Focus and selection](../../references/focus-and-selection.md). Inspect platform/input, focus groups, selected state, dynamic content, and supplied implementation. Establish design/review/adaptation mode. The guide's component-focus model excludes iOS/watchOS; visionOS gaze hover is a different system.

Map focus movement separately from activation and persistent selection. Focus may select automatically only when that does not unexpectedly shift context; tvOS normally needs separate activation. Use system effects and avoid moving focus without input. If an item disappears during discrete directional movement, choose a nearby one-step target; for other input, hide the indicator rather than inventing the next destination.

On iPad, group custom content so Tab moves among logical groups and arrows move within them in expected reading order; prioritize the likely entry item. Ordinary content focus coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls. On TV, every interactive item needs directional reachability and room for enlarged focus art. Keep unfocused, focused, pressed, selected, and unavailable states distinct. Full-screen gestures should manipulate visible content rather than invisible focus.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a TV watchlist opens each item as focus passes over it and uses the same glow for focus and Saved. Decision: navigation must not activate content, and persistent choice must survive focus movement. After, focus raises/highlights the item, Select opens it, and a filled saved indicator remains as focus moves; unavailable items are inactive and unreachable.

Deliver a focus-route/group map and state contract or implementation. Walk each entry, direction, activation, return, and removal scenario. Fail if a control cannot be reached/exited, focus jumps without input, selected state vanishes with focus, or enlargement obscures information. Source inspection can establish intended grouping; actual focus engines, remote behavior, and Full Keyboard Access need supported execution.

Use [Remotes](../apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md) for TV button meanings, [Keyboards](../apple-hig-keyboards/SKILL.md) for shortcuts/access, or [Eyes](../apple-hig-eyes/SKILL.md) when the request actually concerns gaze feedback.

# Focus and selection Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Focus visually identifies an interaction target for component-based navigation with keyboards, remotes, and controllers. Focus can select an item automatically, except where selection would shift context; tvOS normally requires separate activation. Rings/highlights on tablet/Mac and depth/parallax on TV reflect their platform focus models. ## Best practices Use system focus effects unless customization is essential. Do not move focus without input. If a focused item disappears during discrete directional navigation, move to a nearby one-step item; with other input, hide the indicator rather than guessing the next target. Follow platform reachability conventions: keyboard content focus on iPad/Mac coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls, whereas tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item. Use rings for text/search and usually full-row highlights for lists/collections. Standard focused/unfocused selection colors preserve active context. ## Platform considerations The source marks focus unsupported on iOS/watchOS in this topic’s sense. ### iPadOS Since iPadOS 15, Tab moves between focus groups and arrows move inside a group. Group custom views to produce expected reading order, normally leading-to-trailing then top-to-bottom; a vertical stack may need one focus-group container. Set priority so a likely primary item receives focus when a group is entered. Halo effects outline an item and can be refined for shape, clipping, or badge overlap. A content-configured cell’s highlighted accent appearance is separate from a focus effect. ### tvOS In full-screen content, gestures should act on the content rather than invisible focus. Use component focus for menus instead of a tiny free pointer; a gameplay-specific pointer must be conspicuous and integrated. Allow room and high-resolution art for enlarged focus states. Represent unfocused (receded), focused (raised/lit/moving), pressed (immediate feedback), selected (persistent choice such as filled favorite), and unavailable (inactive and unreachable) states distinctly. ### visionOS Connected keyboards/controllers use the same focus system family. Looking at content uses hover feedback instead; do not treat gaze hover as keyboard/controller focus. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Preserve deliberate remote actions across browsing and playback

Read [Remotes](../../references/remotes.md). Inspect the TV hierarchy, playback/game state, remote mappings, and requested design/review/adaptation. This is tvOS-specific. Preserve the existing stack and distinguish a remote press from accidental surface contact or movement.

Map swipes to predictable directional focus/scrolling with corresponding feedback; strength can govern scrolling momentum. Use presses for deliberate activation. Avoid acting on taps during live playback because passing or resting a remote can produce them. Press-then-swipe enters scrubbing; preserve the relationship between gesture and visible media position.

Define Back by hierarchy and task state. In ordinary browsing, Back opens the parent, not necessarily the last screen visited; root returns Home. During gameplay, Back may open a pause menu, Back from that menu resumes, and an additional deliberate action can leave for the game menu. Holding Back retains its system Home behavior. Play/Pause must control active media; game-specific secondary/skip use needs appropriate context.

If an electronic program guide exists, guide/browse buttons open it and page buttons navigate it. During playback, those page requests change channels. Without a guide, preserve system routing to the default guide app rather than inventing unrelated meanings.

**Before → decision → after:** A streaming app treats every clickpad tap as Pause and makes Back jump to a recently searched page rather than the show's parent. Decision: accidental touches should not interrupt viewing and hierarchy must remain predictable. After, deliberate Play/Pause controls playback, presses activate, and Back from the episode returns to its show; guide/page behavior follows the active context.

Deliver a state-by-button/gesture mapping and corrected interaction artifact. Walk browse, play, scrub, pause, and return routes. Fail if incidental contact changes playback, Back strands the person or exits unexpectedly, or a program-guide button performs an unrelated action. Actual Siri Remote gestures, momentum, and across-room feedback need hardware testing; keyboard simulation is partial evidence.

Use [Focus and selection](../apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) for directional reachability or [Game controls](../apple-hig-game-controls/SKILL.md) for controller/menu consistency.

This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. The Siri Remote combines physical buttons and a touch-sensitive clickpad for tvOS navigation, selection, and playback across the room. ## Best practices Preserve standard gestures and focus direction outside specialized gameplay. Provide clear feedback connecting gesture to content. Presses indicate deliberate activation; resting/moving/passing the remote can cause accidental taps, so avoid acting on taps during live playback. Positional up/down/left/right taps can help only when intuitive and discoverable. Back normally opens the hierarchy’s parent, which is not always the previously visited screen; at the root it returns Home. During play, Back can open a pause menu to avoid accidental exits; Back from that menu resumes, while another deliberate action can return to the game menu. Holding Back reaches Home. Play/Pause must play, pause, or resume active media. ## Gestures Swipe scrolls with momentum based on swipe strength; vertical swipes along an edge accelerate through many items. Press activates or selects, and pressing before swiping enters scrubbing. ## Buttons Touch-surface swipe navigates/changes focus in apps and acts like a D-pad in games. Surface press activates/deepens navigation or acts as the game primary button. Back handles parent/exit or pause/resume according to context. Play/Pause controls media, while games may use it as a secondary action or to skip an intro. ## Compatible remotes For an app with an electronic program guide, guide/browse buttons open it; page-up/down navigate within it, also supported by upper/lower surface taps. Without an EPG, the system sends those requests to the default guide app. While content is playing, page-up/down should change channels rather than page through the guide. ## Platform considerations This source is tvOS-specific and marks the other five platforms unsupported. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance.

# Preserve item identity through layout changes

Read [the collection guide](../../references/collections.md). The workflow is application advice, with documented support qualified by platform.

Inspect actual items, screen/code, target input/platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Determine whether visual recognition or text comparison drives selection; record selection, reorder, insertion, and scrolling behavior only when evidenced. Text-heavy comparison may belong in a list/table rather than a collection.

Choose a familiar row/grid before a custom arrangement. Size cells around meaningful imagery and labels, allowing focus/hover expansion without collision. Retain standard selection/editing interactions and use custom gestures only for a demonstrated task need. For iOS/iPadOS layout changes during manipulation, favor explicit triggers and preserve the person's location and selected item; do not reshuffle a live grid merely because a data property changed. The guide marks collections unsupported on watchOS, so adapt to a suitable list rather than assert parity.

Implement a requested collection or produce a cell/layout/interaction specification; review findings must name affected items or transitions. Specify stable identity and understandable insertion/deletion/reorder feedback as application decisions consistent with the guide.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a wallpaper grid reorders by popularity while someone drags an image, causing the target to move. Decision: dynamic ranking conflicts with manipulation. After: preserve the displayed order during the drag and expose an explicit refresh/sort action; animate a deliberate reorder while retaining selection.

Deliver the artifact and layout-change policy. Verify long labels, odd item counts, focused edge cells, reorder, and deletion of the selected item. Fail for overlapping focused cells, accidental activation during scrolling, or identity/location lost after a layout change. Report native focus/gesture execution separately from inspected logic.

# Design the whole focused unit

Read [the lockup guide](../../references/lockups.md). Lockups are tvOS-specific; the procedure below is application advice for that component, not a cross-platform support claim.

Inspect the supplied content, focus/navigation arrangement, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Identify the atomic unit people choose and its header/content/footer. Obtain both focused and unfocused states or mark expansion/tilt unknown.

Choose a card for combined review/rating content, caption button for titled content, monogram for a person, or poster for artwork-led choice. Keep dimensions consistent within a logical group while fitting the actual content. A monogram should prefer an available portrait with initials as fallback. A poster's optional title/subtitle can appear on focus; essential identity must remain understandable in context. Set caption-button focus tilt to the row, stack, or grid navigation direction and reserve enough space for the entire unit's expansion without neighboring overlap.

Implement the lockup, provide focused/unfocused annotated layouts, or report concrete expansion and identity defects. For adaptation to another platform, retain the content relationship using an appropriate supported component rather than calling it a native lockup.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a TV cast grid scales portraits alone while their names remain stationary and the focused portrait covers its neighbor. Decision: portrait and labels are one focusable person. After: group them as monograms that grow together, use consistent cell sizing, and reserve expansion space; missing portraits use initials.

Deliver the chosen form, focus bounds, content hierarchy, and activation outcome. Navigate every edge/corner and verify neighboring content, readable labels, and fallback identity. Fail for overlapping focus states, header/footer detached from content, or inaccessible unnamed choices. Linux layout inspection cannot prove remote-input tilt or native TV focus behavior.

# Preserve readable hierarchy as text grows

Read [Typography](../../references/typography.md). Inspect the actual text roles, font files/styles, platform, viewing context, and resizing behavior. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Use the guide's platform style/size tables when exact values matter; do not reproduce the entire specification or confuse its minimum with a comfortable default.

Assign semantic roles before choosing sizes: title, body, supporting detail, and actionable label need a clear relationship. Prefer system text styles and runtime font APIs so optical design/tracking adapt to size. If a custom face is needed, verify weight/legibility and provide equivalent text-size and Bold Text behavior; thin faces may need more size than the table suggests. Use loose leading for sustained/wide reading, avoiding tight leading across three or more lines.

Decide how content expands. Grow containers, permit labels to wrap, stack timestamps/glyphs, and reduce columns rather than aggressively truncating essential reading. Scale meaningful glyphs with the text. Preserve hierarchy while prioritizing the content people intend to read; not every decorative/transient number must grow identically.

Apply platform differences: macOS has no Dynamic Type, so use appropriate standard-control fonts and explicit product text accommodations rather than promising that API behavior. On visionOS, favor readable 2D text, explicit styles for New York, little extrusion, and viewer-facing object labels; do not rely on cast shadows against unpredictable surroundings. Watch uses its own font conventions, including complication typography.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a book list fixes custom thin titles to one line and leaves status glyphs tiny at larger text sizes. Decision: reading and status must remain usable together. After, titles use a legible role/weight, wrap into growing rows, supporting text stacks, and meaningful glyphs scale while selection/actions stay available.

Deliver corrected type roles, resizing rules, or implementation with supported-size examples. Fail if essential content is clipped without a full-text route, hierarchy collapses, or Bold Text/custom sizing breaks controls. Record tested sizes and actual font measurements; device-distance legibility, native shaping, and spatial comfort need supported execution.

Use [Layout](../apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for reflow, [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for task-level access, or [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for mixed-script alignment.

Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. New York is a complementary serif family. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. SF offers widths such as Condensed/Expanded and weights from Ultralight through Black; equivalent SF Symbol weights enable precise matching. Use semantic text styles to express hierarchy through coordinated weight, size, and leading, and to inherit Dynamic Type/accessibility adjustments where supported. Modify symbolic traits for emphasis or line spacing when justified. Loose leading supports long passages or wide columns; tight leading can fit constrained rows, but avoid it for three or more lines. Access system fonts through platform APIs (`default`, `serif`, and the font-design constants), without embedding the files. Preserve useful information at the largest accessibility size rather than aggressively truncating. Give labels enough lines and avoid truncation in scrolling regions unless a detail view exposes the full text. description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform interfaces for text enlargement, sensory access, assistive input, motor access, cognitive needs, or accessibility preferences.

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Preserve playback intent across entry and exit

Read [the video guide](../../references/playing-video.md). This workflow is application advice; the source's overlapping 2:1 aspect endpoint must not become an invented exclusive rule.

Inspect content aspect/duration, controls, resume state, entry/exit destinations, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Identify system-player use versus a justified custom need. Record real transport/keyboard/remote behavior; a poster or mock control does not prove playback support.

Prefer system players and preserve original aspect without baked-in bars. Use system aspect behavior at the source's ambiguous boundary. Keep useful metadata unobtrusive and extra actions close to playback. Honor Space/remote conventions and secondary-audio hints. For TV-app entry begin/resume the requested content directly with its supplied profile, preparing an in-app exit destination immediately so even a quick exit is coherent. Avoid unnecessary splash/detail barriers and show honest loading only when needed. On TV keep overlays restrained and use the documented delay before an interactive overlay pauses playback. On visionOS start by choice in a modest resizable window, never force immersion, and preserve system control space; inline video remains 2D. Watch clips should be short with suitable unscaled assets rather than a phone player compressed onto the wrist.

Implement playback/entry/exit states or supply transport/aspect/resume specifications; reviews identify exact control, crop, or context failures. Keep encoding/dimension tables in the reference.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a TV-app launch opens a branded detail screen, restarts a long film, and exits to nowhere when Back is pressed quickly. Decision: the playback request already carries intent. After: resume directly at the retained position/profile and prepare the corresponding in-app detail/menu before playback begins.

Deliver the artifact and entry, resume, controls, aspect, loading, and exit contract. Verify quick exit, PiP, different aspect ratios, interruption, overlays, and supported input. Fail for lost resume position, baked-in cropping/bars, forced immersion, or a missing exit context. Native media, audio routing, captions, and comfort need runtime/device evidence.

Load [playing-audio](../apple-hig-playing-audio/SKILL.md), [going-full-screen](../apple-hig-going-full-screen/SKILL.md), or [live-viewing-apps](../apple-hig-live-viewing-apps/SKILL.md) as required.

# Playing video Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-video) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Prefer system players for familiar playback, aspect modes, PiP, and accessible controls. Native players exist in iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, and visionOS, with TV-app integration for supported content. The source defines aspect-fill as the default for wide 2:1–2.40:1 video, potentially cropping edges, and aspect-fit for 4:3, 16:9, up to 2:1, and beyond 2.40:1, preserving the full image with bars as needed. Its exact 2:1 endpoint overlaps both statements; use system player behavior instead of inferring an exclusive boundary. TV and visionOS add transport actions and informational content tabs; spatial transport controls appear in an ornament. ## Best practices Use standard player behavior even when a genuine need requires customization. Preserve the original aspect ratio without baking in letterboxing/pillarboxing, which breaks scaling and PiP. Add only useful metadata that does not obscure playback. Honor ordinary controls, including Space to play/pause with a keyboard and expected remote gestures. Keep extra actions to a step or two; use transport controls for playback-related actions and tabs for supplemental information/recommendations. Handle secondary-audio hints so switching video/PiP and another app does not create unwanted audio mixing. ## Integrating with the TV app Match the TV app's black transition and begin/resume content directly, avoiding splash/detail screens or intro barriers. Rare required interstitials should allow Select to advance and Play to skip to content. Resume long videos at their prior stop time without asking. Honor a supplied viewer profile automatically; if absent, ask once to establish it for later. Keep Space play/pause available. ### Loading content Avoid a loading screen for quick starts. Beyond about 2 seconds, a black screen with a centered spinner and minimal other content can communicate waiting. Begin once sufficient content is ready and stream the rest in the background; any branding should remain minimal against black. ### Exiting playback Playback exits into the app, not back to TV. Show related details with resume, or a containing menu/main menu when details are unavailable. Prepare this exit context immediately after receiving the playback request so even a rapid exit is coherent. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, or macOS rules are specified. ### tvOS Keep noninteractive overlays small and brief; translucent SDR graphics reduce distraction and image-retention risk compared with bright opaque graphics. For interactive overlays, use a minimum 0.5-second delay before pausing media and presenting the overlay, and clearly offer dismissal/resumption afterward. ### visionOS Let the person start playback, begin in a modest resizable window, and keep surroundings visible for comfort. Do not automatically launch fully immersive video. In immersion, preserve the system's predictable player placement and keep virtual objects away from its controls. For scrub previews, provide 160-pixel-wide thumbnails. Inline video is 2D and should leave window content around it rather than filling the window and implying an immersive player; its controls share the plane. RealityKit video suits splash/transitional effects that need no standard playback integration and supports correct 2D/3D aspect and captions. ### watchOS System playback supports short foreground clips, inline or in a separate interface. Prefer clips no longer than 30 seconds to limit storage and wrist fatigue. Avoid scaling assets. Recommended encoding is H.264 High Profile, 160 kbps up to 30 fps; 208×260 px fullscreen portrait or 320×180 px 16:9 landscape; audio 64 kbps HE-AAC. A poster should represent actual content and invite playback without imitating an unrelated system control. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Playing audio](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-audio) [Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback) #### Developer documentation — AVFoundation [HTTP Live Streaming](https://developer.apple.com/streaming/) #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: September 12, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Preserve readable hierarchy as text grows

Read [Typography](../../references/typography.md). Inspect the actual text roles, font files/styles, platform, viewing context, and resizing behavior. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Use the guide's platform style/size tables when exact values matter; do not reproduce the entire specification or confuse its minimum with a comfortable default.

Assign semantic roles before choosing sizes: title, body, supporting detail, and actionable label need a clear relationship. Prefer system text styles and runtime font APIs so optical design/tracking adapt to size. If a custom face is needed, verify weight/legibility and provide equivalent text-size and Bold Text behavior; thin faces may need more size than the table suggests. Use loose leading for sustained/wide reading, avoiding tight leading across three or more lines.

Decide how content expands. Grow containers, permit labels to wrap, stack timestamps/glyphs, and reduce columns rather than aggressively truncating essential reading. Scale meaningful glyphs with the text. Preserve hierarchy while prioritizing the content people intend to read; not every decorative/transient number must grow identically.

Apply platform differences: macOS has no Dynamic Type, so use appropriate standard-control fonts and explicit product text accommodations rather than promising that API behavior. On visionOS, favor readable 2D text, explicit styles for New York, little extrusion, and viewer-facing object labels; do not rely on cast shadows against unpredictable surroundings. Watch uses its own font conventions, including complication typography.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a book list fixes custom thin titles to one line and leaves status glyphs tiny at larger text sizes. Decision: reading and status must remain usable together. After, titles use a legible role/weight, wrap into growing rows, supporting text stacks, and meaningful glyphs scale while selection/actions stay available.

Deliver corrected type roles, resizing rules, or implementation with supported-size examples. Fail if essential content is clipped without a full-text route, hierarchy collapses, or Bold Text/custom sizing breaks controls. Record tested sizes and actual font measurements; device-distance legibility, native shaping, and spatial comfort need supported execution.

Use [Layout](../apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for reflow, [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for task-level access, or [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for mixed-script alignment.

Enlarge hard-to-read text, improve foreground/background contrast, or choose a more legible face. Prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold over Ultralight/Thin/Light, especially at small sizes. Thin custom faces often need sizes above the recommendations. |Platform|Default|Minimum| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| ## Conveying hierarchy Combine size, weight, and color to distinguish levels, and preserve those relationships as text grows. Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. New York is a complementary serif family. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. SF offers widths such as Condensed/Expanded and weights from Ultralight through Black; equivalent SF Symbol weights enable precise matching. Use semantic text styles to express hierarchy through coordinated weight, size, and leading, and to inherit Dynamic Type/accessibility adjustments where supported. Modify symbolic traits for emphasis or line spacing when justified. Loose leading supports long passages or wide columns; tight leading can fit constrained rows, but avoid it for three or more lines. Access system fonts through platform APIs (`default`, `serif`, and the font-design constants), without embedding the files. Runtime tracking adapts by size automatically; mockups may need the tracking values below. ## Using custom fonts Check custom faces against platform size recommendations and actual conditions. Implement Dynamic Type and Bold Text behavior equivalent to the system faces. # Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Lockups Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lockups) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A tvOS lockup combines content, a header above it, and a footer below it into one focusable unit; all parts grow and shrink together as focus changes. Available forms include cards, caption buttons, monograms, and posters. ## Best practices Reserve enough spacing for the focused unit to expand without displacing or overlapping neighbors. Keep dimensions consistent within a row or logical group. ## Cards Use a card's combined header, content, and footer to present media ratings or reviews. ## Caption buttons A caption button presents image or text content with a title and optional subtitle below. Match focus tilt to the navigation arrangement: vertical movement for vertical stacks, horizontal movement for rows, and both axes for grids. ## Monograms Identify people with a circular portrait and name; use initials as a fallback when no portrait exists. Prefer a real image when available because it creates a stronger connection to the person. ## Posters A poster presents an image; optional title and subtitle appear upon focus. # Cooking-video catalog for Apple TV

Platform: tvOS. Browse cooking videos from the sofa, inspect a recipe, deliberately play or resume it, and return to the same catalog position. Preserve existing video IDs, titles, artwork, descriptions, ordering, and progress. Siri Remote alone must complete the task; no phone, voice, controller, touch target, or pinch gesture is required. Framework choice remains open.

## Catalog and reading

Use a vertically scrolling three-column collection at default text size. Each recipe is one caption-button lockup: representative landscape artwork, always-visible title, and duration when available. Artwork and captions focus and enlarge together. Missing artwork uses a neutral placeholder with the same title and dimensions. Details exposes the full title, description, artwork, duration, and Play or Resume action.

Prefer SF Pro semantic tvOS styles: screen title Title 2 (57 pt reference), recipe titles Headline (38 pt), body and action labels Body (29 pt), duration Caption 1 (25 pt). Use platform font APIs rather than frozen pixel sizes. The local guide gives tvOS default text as 29 pt and minimum as 23 pt; the minimum is not the default target. Remove 12-point labels.

Allow two title lines in the default collection; expose unabridged text in details. Support enlargement through at least 200% and Bold Text: grow labels, reduce to two or one columns, and wrap full details in a remote-scrollable reading area. Keep every action reachable. This replaces pinch zoom.

Initial product layout targets: 48 pt between lockup bounds and at least 32 pt expansion clearance at viewport edges, within system safe areas. Increase spacing or reduce columns if actual system focus expansion needs more room. No focused artwork or caption may overlap neighbors or clip. Action buttons have at least 66 × 66 pt activation areas and sufficient width for complete labels. Column counts and spacing are design choices requiring validation, not Apple-prescribed constants.

## Focus and input contract

Use system tvOS focus highlighting and enlargement. Focus shows location and available action without opening details or starting media. Keep unfocused, focused, pressed, persistent progress, and unavailable states distinct. Unavailable recipes display “Unavailable” and cannot activate. No nested tiny artwork controls or hover-only actions.

| Location | Input | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh catalog | Entry | Focus first available recipe |
| Catalog | Left / Right | Adjacent available recipe in the row; no edge wrap |
| Catalog | Up / Down | Nearest column in adjacent row; clamp to available cell in short final row; scroll target fully into view |
| Catalog edge | Direction without candidate | Retain visible focus, no activation |
| One-column layout | Up / Down | Previous / next recipe; Left / Right retains focus |
| Recipe | Select press | Store catalog return state, open details, focus Play/Resume |
| Details | Down from Play/Resume | Enter description reading region if overflowing; Up at its top returns to the action |
| Details action | Select press | Start or resume selected video in system player |
| Player | Play/Pause | Control active media |
| Player | Press then swipe | Standard system scrubbing with visible position feedback |
| Player | Back | Dismiss transient controls as the system requires, then exit to this video's details focused on Resume/Play |
| Details | Back | Containing catalog, same recipe and scroll anchor |
| Root catalog | Back | System Home behavior |
| Any location | Hold Back | Preserve system Home behavior |

Directional swipes provide predictable focus/scroll feedback. Incidental clickpad contact must not activate playback. Every interactive region needs a directional entry and exit; the description cannot trap focus. Browse Play/Pause does not start a merely focused recipe.

## State and playback

Before opening details retain "'`{videoID, catalogOrder, scrollAnchor, column}`. Restore by stable ID rather than index. Do not reorder under active browsing; apply refreshed ordering on a later catalog entry while retaining identity. If the return recipe was removed, choose the next available recipe in retained order, then the previous. If none remain, show “No cooking videos available.” A text-size layout change retains identity and visible anchor, although its column may change.

Retain `{videoID, playbackTime}` separately, updated on pause, exit, and interruption. Backgrounding suspends playback and saves route, focus, and progress; foregrounding restores context without restarting sound. Resume uses the stored time; completed videos offer Play from the beginning.

Focus shows static artwork indefinitely: no video previews, sound, or next-video autoplay. Only explicit Play/Resume activation starts playback. Prefer the system tvOS player with standard transport, caption, audio-track, and aspect controls. Preserve original aspect ratio without baked-in bars or stretching; retain system aspect behavior at the local source'"'s overlapping exact 2:1 boundary. Do not add custom interactive overlays. Playback completion returns to details.

During loading retain chosen video identity and a working Back exit. On failure show “Video couldn't load,” Retry, and Back; Retry repeats the same video/time request. Catalog loading placeholders are not focus targets; failure offers Retry, and empty results show a clear message. Retry is initially focused on an error screen; Back returns to its containing context.

Offer supplied captions through system player controls; do not imply unavailable tracks exist. Caption coverage for dialogue/important cooking sounds and descriptions of visual-only instructions require a content audit. Personal progress is not exposed on anonymous shared screens. If an existing profile system is retained, scope progress and return state by profile and switch to the matching app profile on a system-viewer change. Never reuse another viewer's personal state. New authentication and discovery integrations are outside this adaptation.

## Acceptance contract

On supported tvOS hardware, traverse every row, edge, short final row, reading-region boundary, and recovery action using Siri Remote. Confirm visible focus, no clipping, no traps, and activation only by deliberate press. Dwell on each recipe for 30 seconds: no media or sound starts. Open a scrolled recipe, play/pause/scrub, exit to details, and return to that recipe and scroll anchor. Repeat after interruption, removal, refresh, and enlarged text.

Check long titles, missing artwork, default and 200% text, and Bold Text. Read at 8 feet or farther in realistic television lighting. Measure actual contrast and focus visibility, including Increase Contrast. Verify supported assistive traversal and captions along the complete browse → details → play → return task. These are required execution checks, not results established by this specification.

## Guidance basis

Local installed snapshot only; official links provide attribution without online verification:

- [Designing for tvOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-tvos#Best-practices): distant viewing, remote focus, shared viewers.
- [Typography](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography#tvOS-built-in-text-styles) and [Accessibility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility): platform text sizes, enlargement, controls, sensory alternatives.
- [Collections](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/collections) and [Lockups](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lockups): familiar collection, atomic focus units, expansion clearance.
- [Focus and selection](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#tvOS) and [Remotes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes): directional reachability, deliberate activation, standard button meanings.
- [Playing video](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-video): system controls, original aspect, resume, coherent exits.
